text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes treatment options center on lifestyle changes, oral or injectable medications, and surgical or monitoring approaches.
snippet_highlighted_words: lifestyle changes, oral or injectable medications, and surgical or monitoring approaches

list.snippet: Dietary Changes: Focus on whole foods, non-starchy vegetables, lean proteins, and complex carbohydrates while managing overall calorie intake. Weight management approaches can help improve insulin sensitivity.
Physical Activity: Engage in regular aerobic and resistance exercise to help muscles take up glucose and lower blood sugar.
Metformin: Typically prescribed as a first-line oral medication; it reduces glucose production in the liver and improves insulin sensitivity.
Sulfonylureas (e.g., glipizide, glimepiride): Stimulate the pancreas to produce more insulin.
DPP-4 Inhibitors (e.g., gliptins): Enhance hormone actions that stimulate insulin release and lower post-meal blood sugar.
SGLT2 Inhibitors: Help the kidneys remove excess glucose through urine while offering heart and kidney benefits.
GLP-1 Receptor Agonists & Dual GLP-1/GIP Agonists: Injectable medications that slow digestion, promote fullness, assist with weight management, and reduce cardiovascular risks.
Thiazolidinediones (TZDs) (e.g., pioglitazone): Improve insulin sensitivity in muscle and fat cells.

Insulin Therapy: Used when other treatments no longer keep blood sugar in range or when natural insulin production declines significantly; available in long-acting, short-acting, or pre-mixed forms via pens, syringes, or pumps.
Weight-Loss (Bariatric) Surgery: Can be an option for adults with a higher BMI or co-existing conditions to help manage or put type 2 diabetes into remission.
Blood Sugar Monitoring: Tracking levels via home blood glucose meters or continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) systems.
